subject: [PATCH v7 0/6] fuse: add io-uring buffer pools and zero-copy

reviews.author: Joanne Koong (author)
reviews.summary: The author is addressing a merge conflict in the io-uring patches, specifically in the io_uring/rsrc.c file where the code for registering request buffers was split into two versions. She provides a patch to resolve the conflict by reverting one of the changes and explains that this series is ready for the upcoming merge window.

2026-08-14.patch_summary: This patch series adds support for io-uring buffer pools and zero-copy to the FUSE file system, allowing servers to pass in a contiguous chunk of memory that the kernel can use to service requests. This reduces memory usage requirements and enables optimizations for assigning payload memory to requests. Additionally, it introduces zero-copy functionality, which allows direct access to client pages or page cache folios without copying data through an intermediary buffer, requiring CAP_SYS_ADMIN privileges and using buffer pools.

reviews.author: Bernd Schubert
reviews.summary:
Reviewer Bernd Schubert noted that the new name of the feature is a bit confusing and prefers the previous name, suggesting it could be updated at a later time.

Reviewer Bernd Schubert suggested updating the patch description to start with 'conditions that don't allow io-uring zero-copy' and noted this can be done later, implying it's a minor suggestion.

Gave Reviewed-by
reviews.raw_body:
I notice a bit late, the new name is a bit confusing, the previous name
was easier to read for the intent, but we can update that any time later.

---

Also spotted too late and can updated later, I think it should start
with "conditions that don't allow io-uring zero-copy".

reviews.author: Miklos Szeredi
reviews.summary: Reviewer Miklos Szeredi noted that the io-uring patches were not bound for -next and suggested cherry-picking them instead.
reviews.raw_body:

bound for -next.

Thanks,
Miklos

reviews.author: Jens Axboe
reviews.summary: Reviewer Jens Axboe noted that he had previously staged the patches for Linux kernel version 7.2, but was unaware of the plan to move them to 7.3 and therefore did not create a new branch for it; he agreed that picking the patches from the 7.2 branch is acceptable.
reviews.raw_body:
Right, I had them staged for 7.2 for Joanne, but then wasn't fully aware

never did a new branch for that, picking them from the 7.2 branch is
fine.

-- 
Jens Axboe
